chunks: From him, from al-Naḍr ibn Suwayd, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sinān, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:

I heard him saying: Indeed, the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم slept, and his eyes overcame him, and he did not awaken until the heat of the sun troubled him. Then he awoke and performed two rakʿahs, then he performed the morning prayer, and he said: “O Bilāl, what is with you?” Bilāl said: “The One who caused you to sleep caused me to sleep, O Messenger of Allah.” He said: And he disliked remaining there, and said: “You slept in the valley of a shaytan.”

So the proper way regarding these two reports is that we understand them as applying to one who intends to lead a people in prayer and is waiting for their gathering; in that case, it is permissible for him to begin with the two rakʿahs of nafilah, as the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم did. But if he is alone, then that is not permissible for him in any situation.

key_terms.النَّافِلَةِ: Supererogatory prayer performed in addition to the obligatory prayer.
key_terms.بِلَالُ: Bilāl, whom the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم addressed after awakening.
key_terms.رَكْعَتَيْنِ: Two units of prayer performed before the obligatory prayer in this report.
key_terms.وَادِي شَيْطَانٍ: A valley described as a place associated with shaytan.
key_terms.يُصَلِّيَ بِقَوْمٍ: To lead a group of people in prayer.

ai.seo_question: If someone has missed an obligatory prayer, may they perform nafilah before making up the faridah?
ai.summary: This hadith reports that the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, after oversleeping the morning prayer, performed two rakʿahs before praying al-ṣubḥ. The concluding legal explanation restricts this allowance to a person waiting to lead a congregation, while ruling that a person praying alone may not begin with the nafilah when an obligatory prayer has been missed.
